advisory.title: Pre-shared key mode transmits the TGK in cleartext, exposing the SRTP master key
advisory.description:
`mykey` implements MIKEY (RFC 3830) for SRTP key exchange. Pre-shared key mode
transmitted the TEK Generation Key (TGK) in the clear.

`MikeyMessage::new_psk_init` built its KEMAC payload with `EncAlg::Null` and
placed the TGK in `enc_data` verbatim. Anyone able to read a PSK-Init message
therefore recovers the TGK — and so the SRTP master key — **without knowing the
pre-shared key**.

The transmitted value was never even used by the receiver: `complete_psk`
re-derived the TGK from the pre-shared key and ignored `enc_data` entirely. The
field was write-only; it provided nothing and disclosed everything.

A second consequence: the message authentication key was derived from the TGK
rather than from the pre-shared key, so an attacker who read the TGK off the wire
could also forge a valid message MAC. Integrity was lost along with
confidentiality. That aspect is tracked separately as GHSA-xq78-wvcv-hqvj.

## Exploitability

A MIKEY message is normally distributed as an SDP `a=key-mgmt:mikey` attribute,
which in AES67 and SMPTE ST 2110 deployments is typically announced over SAP
multicast. A passive listener on the media network recovers the session key with
no active attack and no credentials.

RFC 3830 §4.2.3 permits NULL encryption only where "the underlying protocols can
guarantee security", and warns to use it with caution. An SDP file or a SAP
announcement is not such a channel.

## The fix

Pre-shared key mode now follows RFC 3830 §3.1 as key *transport*: the initiator
generates a random TGK, frames it as a Key data sub-payload (§6.13), and encrypts
it with AES-CM (§4.2.3) under an encryption key and 112-bit salt derived from the
pre-shared key (§4.1.4). The message MAC is keyed from the pre-shared key and
verified before anything is decrypted.

This changes the wire format, so both ends of an exchange must be upgraded
together. The incompatibility is silent: an old peer and a new peer complete the
exchange without error and then derive different SRTP keys.

## Workarounds

Use ephemeral Diffie-Hellman mode instead of pre-shared key mode, or carry the
PSK-Init only over a channel that is already confidential and authenticated end
to end.

advisory.title: MIKEY message MAC is never verified on receive, so forged messages are accepted
advisory.description:
`mykey` implements MIKEY (RFC 3830) for SRTP key exchange. No receive path
verified the MIKEY message authentication code.

`crypto::verify_mac` existed and was correct, but it was called only from unit
tests — neither `MikeyMessage::from_bytes` nor `MikeyMessage::complete_psk`
invoked it.

`new_psk_init` computed an HMAC-SHA-1-160 over the serialized message and
appended it, so the tag was present on the wire and looked like integrity
protection. It was decorative: a receiver accepted any message regardless of
whether the MAC was correct, wrong, or absent.

## Consequences

- An attacker able to inject or modify MIKEY messages in transit faced no
  integrity check. Modified RAND, SSRC or security-policy payloads were accepted
  silently. Note that this does not require a man-in-the-middle position: since
  nothing was checked, a wholly forged PSK-Init was accepted.
- Pre-shared key mode therefore provided no mutual authentication, despite the
  documentation claiming that it did. Possession of the pre-shared key was never
  actually proven by either party.
- Replayed init messages were not rejected.

The practical severity was bounded by GHSA-fwjg-cm92-j3hj (cleartext TGK), which
already let a passive observer recover the key material outright without needing
to forge anything.

## The fix

`complete_psk` now verifies the message MAC **before** any decryption, so a
message that fails authentication yields no key material at all. A `MacAlg::Null`
payload, an absent MAC and a truncated MAC are each refused rather than treated
as "no check required".

The authentication key is now derived from the pre-shared key per RFC 3830 §4.1.4
rather than from the TGK — a prerequisite, since verifying against a TGK-derived
key would have been circular while the TGK travelled in the message itself.
Optional §6.9 verification messages were also added, giving the exchange genuine
mutual authentication.

Replay protection is still absent: a captured PSK-Init can be replayed and will
be accepted, because the optional COUNTER timestamp is emitted rather than a
mandatory NTP type and no record of seen timestamps or RAND values is kept. That
gap is tracked at <https://github.com/waxspin/mykey/issues/24> and is not covered
by this advisory.

## Workarounds

Treat parsed MIKEY messages as unauthenticated input: do not rely on pre-shared
key mode for peer authentication or message integrity, and carry it over a
transport that provides both.
